source: DPROD Contracts dprod-contracts/examples/baseline.ttl, policy <https://example.org/offers/customer-api-v1> (EKGF dprod, develop, 50db943)
notes: Extracted unchanged except the anonymous permission is named rule:v1-use. odrl:conflict is absent as in DPROD, so the profile default (odrl:prohibit) applies. This offer's only rule is an unconstrained odrl:use permission, and everything else on the policy — dprod:offerLifecycleStatus dprod:Fulfilled (retired), prov:wasRevisionOf — is metadata: not at any extension point of due2-profiles.md §2, so it is preserved and never evaluated (dprod:effectiveDate/expirationDate are likewise never evaluated in DPROD, formal-semantics.md §3.4 leaving them unmapped). The scenarios therefore show a 'retired' offer still permitting every use: lifecycle status must gate deployment of the policy, not evaluation, in both systems. odrl:read, odrl:display, and odrl:distribute sit under odrl:use in the shipped action hierarchy. DPROD Σ assumed: Σ₀ with clock = request.at. Matching direction: dprod_expected uses the intended §7.4 reading (request ⊑ rule); under the literal reading the use permission never matches a narrower action.

scenarios.name: read customer data under a retired offer

expected.why: odrl:read ⊑ odrl:use, so rule:v1-use matches and is ready. No prohibition exists. dprod:Fulfilled is lifecycle metadata, not evaluated (due2-profiles.md §2), so retirement does not reach the verdict — in due2 or in DPROD.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (the offer has no prohibition and the permission is active; lifecycle status is outside evaluation state, formal-semantics.md §4.1)

scenarios.name: display customer data

expected.why: odrl:display ⊑ odrl:use (shipped hierarchy), so the single permission matches. Permit.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (under the intended §7.4 reading; the literal reading never matches)

scenarios.name: export customer data

expected.why: odrl:distribute ⊑ odrl:use, so even redistribution is permitted by this offer — unlike customer-api-v2, v1 carries no distribute prohibition. The retirement flag is metadata. Both systems read the policy the same way.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (unconstrained use permission; no prohibition in this offer)
